title: Keep only the second-order energy term
spoken: The exact kinetic-energy drop is approximately one half L times the squared ratio v over c, at small speed.
explanation: The approximation sign is essential. Retaining only second order in v/c drops fourth and higher orders; it is not an exact equality at a finite speed.
assumptions: Two equal, opposite light pulses remove total positive energy L; their symmetry removes recoil in the body’s rest frame.
The two inertial descriptions refer to the same emission and the same body boundary; |v| < c.
These are authored modern teaching equations, not a transcription or printed-notation concordance.
The relation H − E = K + C uses the same unknown additive C before and after emission. This is a premise; conservation and subtraction do not prove it.
The observer speed is small compared with c; fourth and higher orders in v/c are omitted.

notes.title: Positive kinetic-energy drop
notes.explanation: ΔK means K₀ − K₁ in this card: before minus after. It is identified from the ledger subtraction only under the unchanged-offset premise.

notes.title: Emitted energy L
notes.explanation: Total energy of both opposite pulses, in the body’s rest frame. It is not the body’s unknown total energy.

notes.title: Multiply the factors
notes.explanation: The coefficient one half comes from the quadratic term in the Lorentz-factor expansion.

notes.title: Same observer speed
notes.explanation: v is the signed relative speed between inertial descriptions. Its magnitude is less than c. It is held fixed while the body emits.

notes.title: Modern SI speed of light
notes.explanation: c denotes the speed of light in modern SI notation. A normalized model with c = 1 is a different unit convention and cannot supply values labeled metres per second.

notes.title: Compare the speed with c
notes.explanation: v/c is dimensionless. Its sign gives the relative direction; squaring removes that direction.

notes.title: Square the speed ratio
notes.explanation: Both positive and negative observer speeds give the same square. The low-speed expansion uses this small dimensionless number.

notes.title: Multiply the factors
notes.explanation: This second-order expression is a low-speed approximation to the exact drop, not an identity.

notes.title: What this relation asserts
notes.explanation: The approximation sign is essential. Retaining only second order in v/c drops fourth and higher orders; it is not an exact equality at a finite speed.

sentence.text: The exact kinetic-energy drop is approximately one half L times the squared ratio v over c, at small speed.
